test_description: Verify that a task with type: ai in its checks list fails at compile/load time with a clear error, preventing LLM-based verification from executing
test_assertions: Task with type: ai check fails at compile/load time
Error message references the Checks, Not Vibes principle
Task with shell-based checks loads successfully
Deprecation warning message is replaced with a hard error
change_description: Replace the AI check dispatch branch (line 536: if (check.type === 'ai')) with a hard rejection that throws at check execution time, structurally preventing the 'Checks, Not Vibes' violation instead of merely warning about it. Remove the runAiCheck() dispatch and associated ai-check.ts import.
why_this_correction: Finding 1 (ai-checks-still-functional) has Correctness dimension — the highest-priority rubric tier. The observe phase evidence shows find-gaps.ts line 536 gates a fully functional AI check branch that dispatches LLM calls through ai-check.ts (229 lines of prompt construction and JSON parsing), directly contradicting the mental model. The deprecation warning is non-blocking — evidence confirms any playbook author can still declare AI checks that execute today. Fixing this makes the Checks, Not Vibes principle structurally enforceable — violations become impossible, not just discouraged. Finding 2 (output-validation-skips-markdown) has Coverage dimension, which is below all rubric tiers; while important, it does not prevent the core anti-pattern of LLM self-judgment.
migration_plan: Playbooks using type: ai checks must replace them with equivalent shell-command checks (test, grep, jq, node scripts) that verify work deterministically. The ai-check module has been deprecated with console.warn since prior epochs — this epoch completes the planned removal per the deprecation schedule.
